\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{छिनत्ति} (chinatti)}{छिनत्ति (chinatti)}]{\sk{छिनत्ति} (chinatti) — cuts}

\label{lesson:SA-C134-chinatti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for swims, then the Sanskrit for jumps.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{छिनत्ति}}
\textbf{\sk{छिनत्ति}} — \emph{chinatti} — \textquotedblleft{}cuts\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{chinatti} comes from the root √chid \textquotedblleft{}cut, split\textquotedblright{}, with the nasal \emph{-na-} that class-7 verbs push inside the root (MW). MW sets √chid beside Greek \emph{schizō} \textquotedblleft{}split\textquotedblright{}, the source of English \emph{schism}, and Latin \emph{scindo}; Gujarati kept it as \emph{chiṇvũ} \textquotedblleft{}to slit\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5045).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chinatti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chinatti}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{chinatti}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for swims, then the Sanskrit for jumps, then say \emph{chinatti} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{भिनत्ति} (bhinatti)}{भिनत्ति (bhinatti)}]{\sk{भिनत्ति} (bhinatti) — breaks}

\label{lesson:SA-C134-bhinatti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for jumps, then the Sanskrit for cuts.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{भिनत्ति}}
\textbf{\sk{भिनत्ति}} — \emph{bhinatti} — \textquotedblleft{}breaks\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bhinatti} comes from the root √bhid \textquotedblleft{}split, break\textquotedblright{}, with the class-7 infix \emph{-na-} (MW). The root is inherited from Indo-European (EtymDB): MW sets it beside Latin \emph{findo} \textquotedblleft{}split\textquotedblright{} and English \emph{bite}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{स्थापयति} (sthāpayati)}{स्थापयति (sthāpayati)}]{\sk{स्थापयति} (sthāpayati) — places, puts}

\label{lesson:SA-C134-sthapayati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for cuts, then the Sanskrit for breaks.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{स्थापयति}}
\textbf{\sk{स्थापयति}} — \emph{sthāpayati} — \textquotedblleft{}places, puts\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sthāpayati} is the causative of the root √sthā \textquotedblleft{}stand\textquotedblright{}: \textquotedblleft{}makes stand, sets up, places\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13756). MW sets √sthā beside Latin \emph{stare} and English \emph{stand}; Bengali kept the causative as \emph{thuoyā} \textquotedblleft{}to put, keep\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13756).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{प्रेषयति} (preṣayati)}{प्रेषयति (preṣayati)}]{\sk{प्रेषयति} (preṣayati) — sends}

Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for breaks, then the Sanskrit for places.

\textbf{\sk{प्रेषयति}} — \emph{preṣayati} — \textquotedblleft{}sends\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{preṣayati} comes from \emph{pra} \textquotedblleft{}forth\textquotedblright{} and the root √iṣ \textquotedblleft{}set in motion, send\textquotedblright{} (MW; CDIAL 9003): \textquotedblleft{}drives on, sends forth\textquotedblright{}. Pali kept it as \emph{peseti} \textquotedblleft{}sends\textquotedblright{}, especially with a message (CDIAL 9003).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{अन्विष्यति} (anviṣyati)}{अन्विष्यति (anviṣyati)}]{\sk{अन्विष्यति} (anviṣyati) — searches}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{अन्विष्यति}}
\textbf{\sk{अन्विष्यति}} — \emph{anviṣyati} — \textquotedblleft{}searches\textquotedblright{}.

\emph{anviṣyati} comes from \emph{anu} \textquotedblleft{}after\textquotedblright{} and the root √iṣ \textquotedblleft{}seek, wish\textquotedblright{} (MW's third √iṣ): \textquotedblleft{}seeks after, searches\textquotedblright{}. It is the same √iṣ as \emph{icchati} \textquotedblleft{}wishes\textquotedblright{}.
